querylog_rule_exists: Rule already exists: {rule} in filter set {set}. Nothing changed.

settings_oidc_viewer: SSO settings are managed by an administrator.

settings_unifi_site_placeholder: Optional when there is only one site
settings_unifi_api_key_set: Set — enter a new key to replace

settings_unifi_insecure_body: The gateway certificate is not checked. Prefer a SHA-256 pin or a CA file. Anyone who can intercept the path to the gateway can inject client names.
config_lead: The full configuration as one atomic snapshot. Check changes before you save them.
config_viewer_only: The full configuration is only visible to administrators. Ask an administrator to make changes here.
config_editor_footer: Secrets are never shown or exported. Saving applies the whole configuration at once.
config_version_none: No configuration version is stored yet.
config_conflict_body: Someone saved a newer configuration. Your text is kept below the editor. Reload the latest version, then apply your changes again.
config_save_blocked: Fix the errors from the last check before you save.
config_parse_error: The JSON is malformed at line {line}, column {column}.
config_not_object: The configuration must be a JSON object.
config_versions_footer: A rollback is recorded in the audit log. The version list does not show who saved a version.
config_rollback_body: The current configuration is replaced by version {version} and applied to all modules. The rollback itself is recorded in the audit log.
config_rollback_done: Rolled back to version {version}. The current version is {current}.
config_import_detail: Loads a JSON file into the editor. Nothing is saved until you save.
config_import_loaded: The file is in the editor. It is being checked, not saved.
config_backups_detail: The control API has no backup endpoint yet. Last run, path and retention appear here once it exists.
config_change_none: No changes compared with the stored version.
config_mcp_carried: Set {set}: {count} MCP rules are carried over (field omitted)
config_mcp_deleted: Set {set}: {count} MCP rules are deleted (empty list)
config_mcp_replaced: Set {set}: MCP rules are replaced by {count} rules
config_check_footer: Checking does not change the config version, is not audited and applies nothing.
zones_lead_tail: to each network. Overlaps: the more specific range wins.
zones_delete_body: Network range {id} is removed. Devices from it fall back to the default range.
zones_id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only. Spaces and _ become -.
zones_range_invalid: Line {line} is not a valid network range (e.g. 192.0.2.0/24 or 2001:db8::/64).
zones_default_delete_blocked: The default network range cannot be deleted.
zones_default_hint: The default range applies to every device that matches no other range. Networks are optional for it. There is exactly one.
zones_pinned_blocked: Cannot be deleted while these Client IDs are pinned here: {names}. Change their range first.
zones_no_subnets: No networks — DoH Client IDs only
zones_empty: No network range yet. A default range makes sure every device gets a profile.
zones_footnote: DoH devices match by IP first; otherwise their Client ID’s range, otherwise the default.
names_lead: Answer and deviations per network range — public when domain zones are attached.
names_delete_body: Remove {name} ({type}) from the global name space.
names_public_hint: Saving updates Cloudflare and the local default.
names_token_banner: Public DNS needs a Cloudflare token.
names_public_internal: Local only — outside attached domain zones.
names_public_absent: Not on Cloudflare yet — save a value to publish.
names_public_unavailable: Public DNS data is not available here.
names_public_error: Could not load the public value.
names_public_proxied_warn: Proxy breaks DoT/DoQ for inventory names — keep DNS-only.
names_public_clear_hint: Clear and save to remove the Cloudflare record.
names_overrides_hint: Only ranges with a different value or no answer. Missing rows inherit the answer above.
names_overrides_empty: None — every range inherits the answer above.
names_overrides_empty_standard: None — every range inherits the answer above.
names_zones_lead: Discover Cloudflare zones and attach apexes. Detach does not delete the zone at Cloudflare.
names_zones_token_missing: Add a Cloudflare token under TLS to discover zones.
names_footnote: Exact names only. CNAME cannot share an owner with other types.
forward_lead: Forward zones send private domains to another DNS server instead of resolving them recursively.
forward_footnote: Forward zones are checked before recursion. Profiles may restrict which forward zones apply.
profiles_lead: Profiles define behavior: filter set, protection (SafeSearch, rebind, AAAA) and schedules.
profiles_schedules_hint: Schedules are stored as UTC week offsets. Local display follows your locale, including daylight saving time.
profiles_footnote: Protection details such as rebind exceptions and forward-zone allow lists are edited in the profile settings.
test_query_lead: Run a query through the policy pipeline without writing to the query log.
test_query_footnote: Test queries do not appear in the query log and do not write to the resolver cache.
clients_lead: Devices from UniFi sync and manual entries. Manual entries override synced names for the same address.
clients_sync_ok: Sync finished · {count} devices · {conflicts} IP conflicts resolved
clients_footnote: UniFi devices are managed by sync. Rename or delete manual entries only.
doh_lead: A Client ID is a name tag for a device that uses DNScraft on the road. Away from home the device usually has an address DNScraft does not know, so the ID in its DoH address identifies it. Treat the ID like a password: anyone who knows it can use DNScraft.
doh_footnote: At home DNScraft recognises devices by their IP address, on the road by their Client ID.
doh_empty: No client ID registered yet. Add one when a device should use DNScraft on the road.
doh_url_no_domain: No public name set. The DoH address appears once one is set in the TLS settings.
doh_url_pending: The DoH address appears once setup is complete (see above).
doh_url_self_signed: The certificate is self-signed. iPhone and Android do not trust it, so the address only appears with a public certificate.
doh_url_invalid: The client ID is invalid, so there is no address.
doh_device_hint: Only for display in the log. Network ranges do not change because of it.
doh_view_none: None — on the road the default network range applies
doh_view_hint: At home the network decides. On the road, when the IP belongs to no network range, this one applies instead of the default.
doh_view_invalid: This network range no longer exists. Choose another one.
doh_roam_default: On the road: default network range
doh_seen_warn: This linked device came from the home network but was assigned to the default network. Check the setup above.
doh_label_hint: To recognise the device, e.g. iPhone von Anna. Up to 64 characters, no duplicates.
doh_id_hint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only, at most 63 characters.
doh_delete_body: Devices that use this client ID are rejected as soon as you delete it.
doh_profile_ssid_hint: Leave empty: DoH applies everywhere, including at home.
doh_server_ips_hint: Helps iOS find the server. If the profile does not work, enter DNScraft's public IP here.
doh_profile_secret: The file contains the client ID. Treat it like a password and do not share it.
doh_profile_err_no_public_domain: No public name set. The profile needs one.
doh_android_hint: Enter this hostname under Private DNS.
doh_check_cert_ok: The certificate comes from a public authority.
doh_check_cert_missing: The certificate is self-signed. Devices do not trust it.
doh_check_record_ok: Record {name} with a home-network address is present.
doh_check_record_missing: No record {name} with a home-network address. At home the request would not arrive from the home network.
doh_record_lan_hint: The address under which DNScraft is reachable in the home network.
doh_record_public_note: Also publish the public address under Names (Öffentlich / Domain zones). DynDNS covers only the inventory hostnames.
filter_rule_raw: Rules as text (AdGuard syntax, one per line)
filter_lists_lead: Block lists from the internet. A filter set decides which of them apply.
filter_lists_refresh_unavailable: List refresh is not available on this node.
filter_lists_used_by_none: Not used by any filter set
filter_lists_delete_question: Delete this list? Filter sets that use it lose it.
listeners_lead: DNS listeners bind protocols and addresses. Public listeners answer only registered client IDs.
listeners_exposure_banner_body: Public listeners expose only registered client IDs—not your whole network.
listeners_id_auto: ID is assigned automatically from protocol and address.
listeners_address_hint: One bind address per listener. For dual-stack, add a second listener (e.g. 0.0.0.0:853 and [::]:853).
listeners_nodes_hint: None selected = bind on every node.
listeners_exposure_public_hint: Only DoT, DoH and DoQ can be public. Plaintext DNS stays local.
listeners_exposure_plaintext_hint: UDP/TCP on port 53 cannot be public — only encrypted protocols.
listeners_footnote: Each listener binds one protocol. Plaintext DNS cannot be public. Use Nodes to scope a listener to specific cluster members.
tls_lead: TLS certificates, ACME and dynamic DNS for your resolver name.
tls_dns_provider_status_hint: ACME DNS-01 and DynDNS use this provider.
tls_dyndns_detected_hint: From the last DynDNS pass on this node. Opt in below to publish each family at Cloudflare.
tls_dyndns_detected_none: Not discovered yet — run DynDNS now or wait for the next interval.
tls_dyndns_publish_v4_hint: Write the detected IPv4 as an A record for this node’s hostname.
tls_dyndns_publish_v6_hint: Write the detected IPv6 as an AAAA record (stable interface id when configured).
tls_engine_unavailable_body: Set a public domain and save, then restart this node so the TLS engine can start. You can edit the configuration below.
tls_dyndns_host_hint: Per-node name for DoH, e.g. {example}. Must be <label>.dns.<domain>.
tls_dyndns_enabled_hint: Master switch: when off, this node does not update Cloudflare at all.
tls_public_entry_hint: Publishes CNAME for dns.<domain> and *.dns.<domain> → this hostname so DoT Client-IDs resolve. Only one node in the cluster.
tls_public_entry_yes: Yes — CNAME apex and wildcard → this host
tls_dyndns_nodes_hint: Opt each node in or out of DynDNS, choose A/AAAA per node, and pick one public-entry for the apex/wildcard CNAMEs.
tls_dyndns_nodes_solo: Standalone: only this node’s hostname is published.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_hint: IPv4 always uses the public echo. Choose how this node picks IPv6.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_mode_eui64_hint: Uses the OS address with a MAC-derived interface id — prefix can change, the host part stays stable.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_mode_stable_hint: Uses the OS stable-privacy address (RFC 7217) — not tied to the MAC, still stable across reconnects.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_mode_static_hint: Publishes a fixed IPv6 you enter below — no discovery.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_help_lead: IPv4 always comes from the public echo service. IPv6 is chosen separately so a changing ISP prefix does not force a new host identity.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_help_eui64_body: Typical for servers with a fixed NIC. The OS builds a global address from the current network prefix plus an interface identifier derived from the MAC. Set an interface (e.g. eth0) so DynDNS reads that address; leave interfaces empty to fall back to the public echo.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_help_stable_body: Same idea as EUI-64 (stable host part, dynamic prefix), but the interface id is a privacy-preserving stable value, not the MAC. Prefer this when you do not want the hardware address in DNS. Also needs an interface name, or uses the echo if none is set.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_help_static_body: You enter the exact AAAA content. Use for manually assigned addresses or when discovery is wrong. No echo and no interface read.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_help_ifaces_body: Comma-separated names on this node (eth0, enp1s0, …). First matching interface with a global IPv6 wins. Empty = ask the public echo for IPv6 as well.
tls_dyndns_ipv6_ifaces_hint: Optional. e.g. eth0 = OS address. Empty = public echo for IPv6 too.
tls_dot_resolve_body: DoH puts the Client ID in the URL path and connects to ns1.dns.… — no per-client DNS name. DoT (e.g. Android Private DNS) uses <id>.dns.… as hostname and SNI, so that name must resolve via CNAME *.dns.<domain> → the public-entry node hostname. There is no cleaner option for stock DoT clients.
tls_source_hint_manual: Upload replaces the active certificate and switches to manual mode.
tls_records_lead: Each node: A/AAAA on its hostname. Public entry: CNAME dns.{domain} and *.dns.{domain} → entry host. Certificate SANs stay dns.{domain} and *.dns.{domain}.
tls_records_names_note: Edit other public DNS records under Names (Domain zones).
tls_record_node_meta: A/AAAA · this node · DoH profiles point here
tls_record_apex_meta: CNAME → {target} · maintained by this public-entry node
tls_record_apex_other: CNAME → public-entry hostname · cluster public-entry node
tls_record_client_meta: DoT only · follows the wildcard CNAME, not a separate DynDNS record
tls_action_renew_detail: Start ACME issuance or renewal immediately
tls_action_rotate_detail: Generate a new leaf key and re-issue
tls_action_preflight_detail: Validate DNS and ACME readiness without changing the cert
tls_action_dyndns_detail: Push the current public IP to Cloudflare
tls_action_upload_detail: Paste a PEM certificate and private key
tls_action_revoke_detail: Revoke the active certificate for every client
tls_upload_hint: Paste PEM material once. Private keys are never shown after upload.
tls_revoke_body: Revocation is destructive and affects every connected client.
tls_confirm_banner_body: Saving can briefly interrupt existing DoT/DoH connections.
tls_private_key_never: Private keys and the Cloudflare API token are never shown after they are stored.
tls_dns_provider_hint: Used for ACME DNS-01 and DynDNS. Cloudflare publishes automatically; Manual means you copy TXT records yourself.
tls_cf_token_hint: Zone:DNS:Edit on the zone that holds dns.<domain>. Stored write-only — never shown again.
tls_cf_token_set: Token is set — leave blank to keep, or clear below.
tls_cf_zone_hint: Optional. Empty = resolve by public domain name via the Cloudflare API.
tls_cf_zones_hint: Optional extra zones (name + optional zone id), resolved by longest suffix match.
tls_cf_manual_hint: With Manual, ACME shows the TXT name/value to publish. DynDNS requires Cloudflare.
tls_cf_none_hint: No DNS provider — ACME DNS-01 and DynDNS cannot run.
cluster_lead: Sub-nodes enrolled in this cluster and their configuration lag.
cluster_standalone_body: Cluster administration is not available on this node.
cluster_join_once: Copy this token now. It cannot be shown again.
cluster_revoke_body: Revoke node {id} from the cluster? The node loses its configuration and its access to the cluster and must join again to work.
mcp_rules_lead: Rules, temporary allows and pauses managed through MCP or the API.
rules_intro: Every rule that blocks or allows a specific domain, from all filter sets, is listed here.
rules_empty_body: No rules yet. A rule blocks or allows a domain in a filter set, or is created over MCP.
rules_read_only: View only. Only an admin can change rules.
rules_mcp_unavailable: MCP-created rules are not available on this node.
rules_remove_missing: This rule is no longer in the filter set. Nothing changed.
rules_resumed: Filtering in filter set {set} is back on.
rules_add_subdomains_meta: Also applies to every subdomain of this domain.
rules_add_domain_invalid: A domain cannot contain spaces, slashes or characters such as ^ | $ *.
rules_add_exists: The rule already exists in filter set {set}. Nothing changed.
rules_no_sets: Rules need a filter set. Create one first.
settings_retention_viewer: Query log retention is managed by an administrator.
settings_ip_truncation_label: IP addresses in the query log
settings_ip_truncation_note: Applies only to queries recorded from now on. Earlier entries keep their full address.
settings_update_unavailable: Update check is not available on this node.
settings_mcp_lead: Model Context Protocol server switches and limits.
settings_mcp_unavailable_body: This build does not expose MCP keys in the versioned configuration snapshot.
settings_mcp_footnote: Changing MCP settings may require a process restart on some builds.
token_plaintext_body: Copy this token now. It cannot be retrieved again.
token_self_signed_banner_body: MCP clients must pin the bootstrap certificate while TLS is self-signed.
token_self_signed_confirm_label: I understand MCP clients must pin the bootstrap certificate
token_self_signed_confirm_required: Confirm the self-signed warning before creating an MCP token.
api_explorer_lead: Documented control-api paths for exploration. Mutations stay disabled here.
filter_sets_intro: A filter set defines what is blocked: lists, your own rules and blocked services.
filter_sets_intro_profiles: assign a filter set to devices.
filter_sets_empty: No filter set yet. A filter set defines what profiles block.
field_id_invalid: The ID may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (1 to 64 characters).
profiles_delete_body: Profile {id} will be removed. Network ranges that use it must be switched to another profile first.
listeners_delete_body: Listener {id} will be removed. Devices that use it for DNS may lose DNS access.
forward_delete_body: Forward zone {zone} will be removed. Queries for it are resolved recursively again.
clients_delete_body: The manual entry {name} will be removed.
clients_ip_invalid: Enter a valid IP address or CIDR range.
doh_label_required: Enter a name so you can recognise the device.
dashboard_paused_body: Filtering is suspended until {time} ({minutes} min left).
error_reason_id_pattern: The ID may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (1 to 64 characters).
error_reason_subnet_overlap: The range {subnet} already belongs to another network range.
error_reason_empty_label: The domain name contains an empty label, for example two dots in a row.
error_policy_config_unknown_filter_set: The filter set does not exist.
error_policy_config_unknown_forward_zone: The forward zone does not exist.
error_policy_record_cname_conflict: This name already has another record. A CNAME cannot coexist with other records.
error_policy_id_empty: The ID must not be empty.
error_policy_id_invalid_char: The ID may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
error_filter_id_empty: The ID must not be empty.
error_filter_id_too_long: The ID is too long (at most 64 characters).
error_filter_id_invalid_char: The ID may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
error_filter_list_url_invalid: The list address is invalid. Only http and https are allowed.
error_resolver_config_invalid: The resolver configuration was rejected. Check the inputs.
error_tls_acme_order: The certificate could not be ordered. The certificate authority rejected the order or was unreachable.
error_tls_acme_order_pending: The certificate order is still in progress.
error_tls_acme_challenge: The certificate authority's domain validation failed.

names_owner_invalid: This is not a valid domain name.
zones_range_duplicate: The range {range} already belongs to network range {view}.
filter_lists_source_invalid: The source must be an http:// or https:// address or a file path.
cluster_edit_id: Node ID {id} stays the same; it is the node's identity in the cluster.
cluster_edit_hint: Leave a field empty to clear it. The host name is the public DNS name of this node.
cluster_edit_host_invalid: Enter a valid host name, e.g. ns1.dns.example.com.
